## Windows MCP Server - Core Workflows

### 1. WINDOW TARGETING (Required First Step)
window_management(action='find', title='...') → returns handle
Use this handle for ALL subsequent operations. Never launch twice - reuse handles.

### 2. UI INTERACTION (Preferred)
ui_snapshot(windowHandle='<handle>') - ORIENT FIRST: compact element tree. REPEATED-CHECK RULE: for before/after or any repeated inspection, you MUST explicitly pass mode='auto' on the first and every later snapshot; never omit mode or choose full. Use full only for one inspection. Use reset then auto to replace an older comparison. parentElementId revisits a known subtree id from an earlier snapshot/find; omit it to inspect the whole window.
ui_find(windowHandle='<handle>', name='...') - discover elements (name, controlType, coordinates)
ui_click(windowHandle='<handle>', name='...' | nameContains='...' | automationId='...' | elementId='...') - click by name or reuse an id from ui_snapshot/ui_find. Add doubleClick=true to double-click an element without coordinates.
ui_type(windowHandle='<handle>', text='...', controlType='Edit') - type into a field (also accepts elementId='...')
ui_select(windowHandle='<handle>', value='...', name='...') - pick a value in a combo box / list / tab
ui_read(windowHandle='<handle>', name='...') - read element text (OCR fallback; also accepts elementId='...')
ui_read_table(windowHandle='<handle>', automationId='...' | elementId='...') - extract a grid/table/details-list into structured rows + headers in ONE call (no OCR, no per-cell ui_read loop)
file_save(windowHandle='<handle>', filePath='C:\path\file.txt') - save via Save As dialog
file_open(windowHandle='<handle>', filePath='C:\path\file.txt') - open an existing file via the Open dialog (file must exist)
Works for: buttons, menus, text fields, checkboxes, combo boxes, standard controls.

### 2b. WAITING (No blind sleeps)
ui_wait(windowHandle='<handle>', mode='appear', nameContains='...') - wait for an element to appear
ui_wait(windowHandle='<handle>', mode='disappear', nameContains='...') - wait for a spinner/dialog to close
ui_wait(mode='state', elementId='...', desiredState='enabled') - wait until an element reaches a state

### 2c. BATCH, MACROS & FUSION (Fewer round-trips)
ui_batch(windowHandle='<handle>', steps='[...]', stopOnError=true) - run many steps (find/click/type/select/wait/read/snapshot/key/mouse/polyline) in ONE call. Use for multi-field forms AND for canvas drawing instead of many separate calls.
ui_macro(action='save', name='...', steps='[...]') then ui_macro(action='run', name='...', windowHandle='<handle>') - persist a ui_batch sequence and replay it later; also action='list'/'get'/'delete'.
ui_click(windowHandle='<handle>', name='...', withSnapshot=true) - add withSnapshot=true to ui_click/ui_type/ui_select to verify the result without another call. Use snapshotMode='full' once, 'auto' for repeated checks, or 'reset' to begin a new comparison.

### 2d. CLIPBOARD (Fast bulk text IO)
clipboard(action='get') - read the clipboard text; clipboard(action='set', text='...') - write it; clipboard(action='clear').
Pair with copy/paste hotkeys: focus app, keyboard_control(key='c', modifiers='ctrl'), then clipboard(action='get'); or clipboard(action='set', text='...') then keyboard_control(key='v', modifiers='ctrl').

### 3. KEYBOARD
keyboard_control(windowHandle='<handle>', action='press', key='s', modifiers='ctrl') - hotkeys
keyboard_control(windowHandle='<handle>', action='type', text='...') - raw text input

### 4. MOUSE OPERATIONS (Canvas/Drawing)
**CRITICAL: Never guess coordinates. Discover them first:**
1. ui_find(...) → returns bounding rectangles and click coordinates for elements
2. screenshot_control(annotate=true) → returns numbered element labels + click coordinates
3. mouse_control(action='drag', x=<discovered>, y=<discovered>, endX=..., endY=...)

**When to use mouse_control:**
- Canvas/drawing areas (no accessibility elements inside)
- Drag operations
- Custom controls ui_click can't click

**Multi-stroke drawing - use ui_batch, not N separate calls:**
ui_batch(windowHandle='<handle>', steps='[{"action":"polyline","points":[[300,200],[500,200],[500,400],[300,200]]}, {"action":"mouse","mouseAction":"drag","x":600,"y":200,"endX":700,"endY":400}]')
- polyline presses once, traces every vertex, releases once - ONE continuous stroke, no pen lift at corners.
- mouse step coordinates are window-relative by default; add target='primary_screen' or monitorIndex for screen-relative.
- The window is auto-activated before each mouse step, so batches don't fail on lost focus.

**Hybrid workflow for drawing apps:**
- Use ui_click to click toolbar buttons (tools, colors)
- Use ui_find to get the canvas bounding rectangle
- Use ONE ui_batch with mouse/polyline steps inside canvas bounds for the drawing itself

### 5. VERIFICATION
screenshot_control(annotate=true) - see current state with element positions
ui_find(...) - confirm expected elements are present after an action
